description: C017 | Conquered polity: Hellenistic Crete (323 BCE to 69 BCE; ended c. 67 BCE) | region: Southeastern Europe | main tradition of the conquered population according to the database: Greek | conquering polity or group: Roman Republic (province of Crete, later Crete and Cyrene)

coder_A.source2: Beatrice Poletti, ''Foreign' Cults at Rome at the Turn of the Principate', Acta Antiqua Academiae Scientiarum Hungaricae 58 (2018) 549-569 - https://real.mtak.hu/104180/
coder_A.notes: Rome annexed Crete 67 BCE (Gortyn capital). Roman state cult was retained; Greek gods were already assimilated before conquest, and Augustus embraced and reshaped Greek cults such as the Eleusinian Mysteries. Patronage alongside Roman cult, not adoption; boundary blurry.

coder_B.source2: Encyclopaedia Britannica, 'Roman religion: Influence on Roman religion' - https://www.britannica.com/topic/Roman-religion/Influence-on-Roman-religion
coder_B.notes: Metellus completed the conquest of Crete (69-67 BCE); it was joined to Cyrene as a province. Roman state religion persisted; its Hellenization (Greek rites, gods, myths) began in the 6th-4th centuries BCE, long before this conquest, so no new adoption followed.

description: C022 | Conquered polity: Later Wagadu Empire (1078 CE to 1203 CE; ended c. 1203 CE) | region: West Africa | main tradition of the conquered population according to the database: Islam | conquering polity or group: Sosso (Susu) kingdom of Sumanguru

coder_A.source2: Encyclopaedia Britannica, 'Ghana (historical West African empire)' - https://www.britannica.com/print/article/232424; Metropolitan Museum of Art, 'The Empires of the Western Sudan: Ghana Empire', Heilbrunn Timeline - https://www.metmuseum.org/toah/hd/ghan/hd_ghan.htm
coder_A.notes: Sumanguru captured Kumbi c.1203 and adhered to Susu traditional religion; Sosso power fell to Sundiata c.1235 without conversion. Database Islam kept but disputed (Met: Ghana's king never fully embraced Islam). Sosso writing unattested.

coder_B.source2: Metropolitan Museum of Art, Heilbrunn Timeline, 'The Empire of Ghana' - https://www.metmuseum.org/toah/hd/ghan/hd_ghan.htm
coder_B.notes: Britannica: Sumanguru's 'enthusiastic adherence to the traditional religion of the Susu' alienated Ghana's predominantly Muslim merchant class after he took Kumbi c.1203. Sosso power was short-lived (ended by Sundiata c.1235). Ghana population only partly Muslim. No evidence of Sosso literacy; known from oral tradition.
